newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold calls for euro costs compensation.
newsitem.headline: Ahold calls for euro costs compensation.

text.p: Retailers should be compensated for the cost of the introduction of a common European currency, an executive with Dutch supermarkets chain Ahold said on Wednesday.

Andre Buitenhuis, senior vice-president for fiscal affairs, told a conference the cost had been calculated at between 1.1 and 1.8 percent of sales, equivalent to a full year's margin for food retailers.
He said increasing retail prices would be impossible as it would affect purchasing power, particularly of lower-income consumers.
Buitenhuis said a solution may be found in corporate income-tax, such as a double-deduction for costs related to the introduction of the euro.
He said Ahold's preferred solution would be a remittance of value-added tax to the amount of the costs, many of which are related to turnover.
He saw this as effective as it would take into account size and sales volumes.
"If European and national governments want the euro introduction to work right from the beginning, they need cooperation of the retailers," he said.
"For retailers, compensation is an absolute condition," Buitenhuis said in a speech to business leaders at a conference on European economic and monetary union (EMU).
The Dutch supermarkets organisation CBL earlier this month estimated the cost of the euro on the sector at 700 million guilders, or 1.5 percent of turnover.
Buitenhuis said the single currency would be felt most intensively in retailing, where most transactions occur, and would have a massive impact on the sector.
He said retailers would have to accept the original currency and the euro for six months in 2002.

Ahold's Albert Heijn chain, with 27 percent of the Dutch supermarket sector, would need an extra 2.5 million extra hours at the check-out because of increased time per transaction when two currencies are in operation.
"We do have to accept the two currencies and we're not pleased to say the least," he said.

"We therefore believe that the introduction has to be a Big Bang operation in a much shorter period of time, to decrease the cost and make the considerable effort expected from retailers realistic and affordable."
